          England vs Spain Prediction: UEFA Nations League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Sep 24, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Saturday's UEFA Nations League action is headlined by a huge clash at Wembley. We look ahead to the game with our England vs Spain prediction and preview.
Before a stirring semi-final fightback from Argentina, arguably aided by some suspect substitutions from Thomas Tuchel, England were on course to meet Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.

Instead, following late goals from Enzo Fernández and Lautaro Martínez, the Three Lions had to contest the third-place play-off with France, edging a frantic encounter 6-4, before watching Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina in the showpiece match from afar.

Having received stern criticism in the wake of that semi-final collapse, Tuchel needs to rebuild some trust with England's fans, and he has a blockbuster fixture to prepare for as Spain visit Wembley Stadium in the UEFA Nations League on Saturday.

England are back in the top tier of the competition after suffering a humiliating relegation to League B in 2022-23, having to fight their way out of the second level in 2024-25. They did so with five wins from six games under interim boss Lee Carsley (L1), with their current three-match winning streak being their longest ever in the competition.

It is important to remember that Tuchel has the best win rate of any England manager to ever lead the team for at least 10 matches, at 77% (P22 W17 D2 L3), while the Three Lions have only averaged more goals per game under Walter Winterbottom (2.8) than Tuchel (2.3).
England have also won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of their most recent five without conceding.

Only once in their history have England's men previously won six consecutive competitive home games to nil, under Roy Hodgson and Gareth Southgate between March 2015 and March 2017. That run also spanned Sam Allardyce's short-lived tenure, but he, of course, never got to lead the team out on home soil.

Tuchel has had to contend with a series of withdrawals ahead of this extended, four-game international break, with Tino Livramento, Kobbie Mainoo, Cole Palmer, Marcus Rashford and Declan Rice all pulling out of England's squad.
Everton's James Garner and Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White, neither of whom made the World Cup squad, have been called up as replacements.

Tuchel was criticised for leaving several creative players at home this summer, so Gibbs-White – whose 13 Premier League goals this calendar year are the joint-most alongside Erling Haaland – will hope to seize his opportunity.

But heavy rotation looks unlikely for Saturday's game, at least, which should provide a useful yardstick for the World Cup bronze medallists. Jude Bellingham has scored seven goals in 10 appearances for England in 2026, with David Platt being the last midfielder to net more for them in a calendar year back in 1993 (eight).

He will reprise his partnership with Harry Kane, who is widely seen as a front-runner for the Ballon d'Or. And with one of Kane's main rivals for the award – Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal – lining up on the other side, that is another storyline to keep an eye on.
Aided by Yamal's brilliance, Spain also reached the final of the 2024-25 Nations League, eventually going down to Portugal on penalties following a 2-2 draw in the final.
Spain's last five Nations League matches have seen them both score 2+ goals and concede 2+ goals, which is the longest run by any nation – in any tier – since the tournament's inception in 2018.

La Roja have reached three of the last four Nations League finals, also losing to France in 2020-21 and beating Croatia on penalties in 2022-23. Excluding spot-kicks, they have lost just one of their last 18 matches in the competition (W10 D7).

And during the last edition of the Nations League, only Cristiano Ronaldo (eight goals) outscored Mikel Oyarzabal (four). The Real Sociedad forward has 26 goal involvements across his last 25 international appearances (19 goals, 7 assists), a run that started with him scoring the winner against England in the Euro 2024 final.

Spain enter the game defending a 38-match unbeaten run in all competitions, winning 29 games and drawing nine in that time. It is the longest ever streak by a European nation, dating back to a 1-0 defeat to Colombia in March 2024, which did take place on English soil, at West Ham United's London Stadium.

Spain's last competitive defeat, which came all the way back in March 2023, also occurred in Britain, as they lost 2-0 to Scotland in a qualifier for Euro 2024. Might that be a positive omen for England?
Spain have won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.
